So I just got back into playing this free mmo and to be honest I don't see what all the negativity is about.

Sure some things are limited to if you pay the $15 per month subscription like land ownership and the ability to list items for auction however if you only pay 1 month you get all of those things and can buy land tax certificates with ingame gold.

Imo it is an awesome game with a deep meta system around trading, piracy, faction wars and activities like fishing and crafting.

Not to mention naval battles.

In my opinion the negativity this game gets is undeserved.

When the game started out you could only loot something like 5 enemies before you had to pay money to buy more "labor", so that was pretty much what caused people to hate the game right off the bat. I heard they made that system a little less insane, but there is honestly just no way to ever regain the good will of gamers at large after pulling a stunt like that.

The bigger issue though is simply that the game is grindy as hell and all that great endgame content is gated behind absurd amounts of upkeep. It's all "Hey, we have kingdom building and naval battles", which is cool and all, but you have to do how many hours of the most mundane, boring WoW grind to ever even get to see that? And then if you want to actually participate in that kind of content you have to show up practically every day, keep a massive flow of resources going and do all kinds of busywork that consumes your life.

Bottom line is: When you design a game that people have to log into every single day for hours in order to get the intended experience out of it then your game no longer competes in the realm of "Is it a fun game?" it competes in the realm of "Is it more fun than everything else I could be doing every single day?", and that's an impossibly high bar to pass for games that aren't head and shoulders above everything else the industry has created up to that point.

Making "hardcore MMOs" is a losing proposition, because hardcore gamers only ever play one game at a time, so you have to compete with every other game on the market for their time. Casual players play all kinds of games and often many at the same time, so all you have to do to attract them is to offer a different experience than other games, rather than a better one. Casual friendly games also don't have to be shallow, they can have all the same depth as a hardcore game, they just need to be playable without having to spend a lot of time to be able to get to the meat and potatoes of the game and they should never punish the player for taking a break from the game because that makes them less likely to pick it back up.

I am one of the people who followed it eagerly and bought the archaeum founder's pack, and I feel I got my money's worth from the alpha and closed beta builds of the game. It was a fun, solid MMO with a massive scale and unmatched level of freedom to customize. Don't get me wrong, the game itself is great fun. I still play on the mail.ru version because it's scaled back to the point you may have an edge if you pay more, but not by a decisive margin. The Korean version I tried before the regional blocking was ok as well, if even more grindy. The Western version is just an unfun cash grab by Trion though. It's pay to win. And I don't use the term lightly.
